question_stem:
An α-particle moves in a straight line through a vacuum with a constant speed of 4.1 × 10^{6} m s^{-1}.
The α-particle enters a uniform electric field at point A, as shown in Fig. 4.1.
The α-particle continues to move in the same straight line until it is brought to rest at point B by the
electric field. The deceleration of the α-particle by the electric field is 2.7 × 10^{14} m s^{-2}.
question_stem_latex:
An α-particle moves in a straight line through a vacuum with a constant speed of $4.1 \times 10^{6}\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$.
The α-particle enters a uniform electric field at point A, as shown in Fig. 4.1.
The α-particle continues to move in the same straight line until it is brought to rest at point B by the
electric field. The deceleration of the α-particle by the electric field is $2.7 \times 10^{14}\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text: State the direction of the electric field.
parts.question_text_latex: State the direction of the electric field.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the distance AB.
distance = m

parts.label: (c)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the electric field strength.
electric field strength = V m^{-1}
parts.question_text_latex:
Calculate the electric field strength.
$electric field strength = V m^{-1} $

parts.label: (d)
parts.question_text:
The α-particle is at point A at time t = 0.
On Fig. 4.2, sketch the variation with time t of the momentum of the α-particle as it travels
from point A to point B. Numerical values are not required.
parts.question_text_latex:
The α-particle is at point A at time t = 0.
On Fig. 4.2, sketch the variation with time t of the momentum of the α-particle as it travels
from point A to point B. Numerical values are not required.

parts.label: (e)
parts.question_text: State the name of the quantity that is represented by the gradient of the graph in (d).
parts.question_text_latex: State the name of the quantity that is represented by the gradient of the graph in (d).

parts.label: (f)
parts.question_text:
A β^{-} particle now enters the electric field along the same initial path as the α-particle and with
the same initial speed of 4.1 × 10^{6} m s^{-1}.
parts.question_text_latex:
A $β^{-}$ particle now enters the electric field along the same initial path as the α-particle and with
the same initial speed of $4.1 \times 10^{6}\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the kinetic energy, in J, of the β^{-} particle at point A.
kinetic energy = J
parts.question_text_latex:
Calculate the kinetic energy, in J, of the $β^{-}$ particle at point A.
$kinetic energy = J $

parts.label: (f)(ii)
parts.question_text:
State and explain the differences between the electric force on the β^{-} particle in the
electric field and the electric force on the α-particle in the electric field.
parts.question_text_latex:
State and explain the differences between the electric force on the $β^{-}$ particle in the
electric field and the electric force on the α-particle in the electric field.

parts.label: (f)(iii)
parts.question_text:
The β^{-} particle is produced by the decay of a nucleus. State the name of another lepton
that is produced at the same time as the β^{-} particle.
parts.question_text_latex:
The $β^{-}$ particle is produced by the decay of a nucleus. State the name of another lepton
that is produced at the same time as the $β^{-}$ particle.
